question: How is rehabilitation different from acute care?

options.A: Acute care focuses on vaccination, while rehabilitation treats chronic illness
options.B: Acute care saves lives and cures disease, while rehabilitation restores independence
options.C: Acute care stops all medication, while rehabilitation starts new drugs
options.D: Acute care provides lifelong shelter, while rehabilitation offers short stays

explanation: Spot on! Acute care is all about handling immediate emergencies and stopping disease, whereas rehabilitation steps in to help patients regain their lost abilities so they can live freely again. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of community-based rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: It completely stops patients from ever visiting a hospital
options.B: It removes the need for support from family members
options.C: It brings healthcare services right into the patient's local environment
options.D: It focuses only on surgical procedures

explanation: You got it! CBR makes care super accessible because it meets patients where they live, making it easier for them to join in and transition back to everyday life. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h1)

question: In rehabilitation, what does 'empowerment' really mean for a patient?

options.A: Supporting patients and their families to make their own choices
options.B: Using expensive imported equipment for all daily exercises
options.C: Making the patient completely dependent on healthcare workers
options.D: Limiting how much a patient is involved in their care plan

explanation: Brilliant! Empowerment means walking alongside patients so they take charge of their own recovery journey instead of just waiting to be told what to do. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h2)

question: When planning community-based rehabilitation, why do we use local materials?

options.A: To ban all physical tools during therapy sessions
options.B: To rely completely on single-use plastics
options.C: To require buying advanced technology from abroad
options.D: To encourage using low-cost, locally available items

explanation: Correct! Sustainable care uses things people can easily find, afford, and fix right in their own neighborhoods without breaking the bank. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h2)

question: Where does primary-level rehabilitation usually happen?

options.B: At large university teaching hospitals only
options.C: At local health posts and primary health centers

explanation: That's right! Primary-level care is the closest healthcare point to the community, handling basic checks and early support right where people live. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h3)

question: A patient has a severe spinal cord injury needing advanced surgery. Where should they be sent?
explanation: Spot on! Complex cases like major spine injuries need specialized tertiary hospitals with advanced equipment and expert surgical teams. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main job of an occupational therapist in a rehab team?

options.A: Managing hospital financial budgets and payroll
options.B: Helping patients master fine motor skills and daily activities
options.C: Prescribing pharmaceutical drugs for acute infections
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries on fractured bones

explanation: Correct! Occupational therapists focus on helping people get back to daily essentials like eating, dressing, bathing, and working. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h4)

question: A stroke patient is having trouble swallowing and speaking clearly. Who should you call first?
explanation: You nailed it! Speech-language pathologists are experts at evaluating and managing speech and swallowing troubles after a stroke. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why should family members be included during a rehabilitation assessment?

options.A: Caregivers often notice daily challenges that clinical tests miss
options.B: Family members are legally required to sign all charts
options.C: Relatives can perform physical therapy instead of professionals
options.D: It reduces the total cost of purchasing hospital equipment

explanation: Great job! Families live closely with the patient, so they give us real-life insights that a quick check in the clinic might completely miss. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a baseline functional assessment before starting rehab?

options.A: To discharge the patient from the hospital immediately
options.B: To prove that the patient cannot recover
options.C: To measure future progress and guide the care plan
options.D: To determine the final cost of medical insurance

explanation: Exactly! The baseline gives us a clear starting line so we can track how much the patient improves over time. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h5)

question: What do the letters in the SMART goal-setting framework stand for?
explanation: Spot on! SMART goals help nurses and patients set clear, realistic, and trackable targets for recovery. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why must nurses weave therapy principles into everyday nursing care?

options.A: To ensure consistent practice and reinforce progress across all shifts
options.B: To shorten the length of the patient's hospital stay
options.C: To replace the physical therapist entirely during night shifts
options.D: To reduce the number of medical documents in the chart

explanation: You got it! Consistency helps patients rebuild their neural pathways and physical strength much faster when practiced all day long. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier faced by patients needing rehabilitation?

options.A: Physical barriers like stairs and narrow doors
options.B: Negative cultural beliefs and social stigma
options.C: Excessive availability of trained therapists in rural areas
options.D: High financial costs for care and equipment

explanation: Correct! Rural areas unfortunately suffer from a serious shortage of healthcare workers, not an oversupply of them. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h7)

question: How can community health nurses best fight social stigma against disability?

options.A: By ignoring cultural beliefs entirely without discussion
options.B: By focusing solely on medication management in clinics
options.C: Through patient advocacy and public health education
options.D: By keeping affected individuals hidden safely at home

explanation: Brilliant! Education and speaking up help clear away harmful myths, replacing fear with inclusion and understanding. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the main goal of periodic evaluation during rehabilitation?

options.A: To permanently discharge the patient from follow-up
options.B: To see if goals are met and adjust interventions if needed
options.C: To punish the patient for slow physical recovery
options.D: To increase the cost of hospital equipment rentals

explanation: Spot on! Regular check-ins let the care team see what is working and tweak the plan if the patient hits a roadblock. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h8)

question: Why is long-term support still needed after active rehabilitation therapy ends?

options.A: To keep hospital bed occupancy rates artificially high
options.B: To ensure the patient remains dependent on healthcare workers
options.C: To help maintain functional gains and prevent secondary complications
options.D: To eliminate the need for home visits by family members

explanation: You nailed it! Ongoing follow-up stops setbacks like pressure sores or joint stiffness, helping individuals hold onto their independence for the long haul. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h8)
